messages.content: What is the time difference between Los Angeles and Berlin?

function.name: get_co_ordinate

message.content:
Los Angeles (Pacific Time) is **9 hours behind** Berlin (Central European Time).

| Period | Los Angeles (UTC offset) | Berlin (UTC offset) | Time difference |
|--------|--------------------------|---------------------|-----------------|
| Standard time (winter) | UTC‑8 (PST) | UTC+1 (CET) | **+9 h** (Berlin ahead) |
| Daylight‑saving time (summer) | UTC‑7 (PDT) | UTC+2 (CEST) | **+9 h** (Berlin ahead) |

Because both regions shift forward and backward by the same amount (one hour) at roughly the same time of year, the 9‑hour gap stays constant throughout the year. Only during the brief transition windows (when one side has switched to DST and the other hasn’t yet) can the difference momentarily be 8 or 10 hours, but for everyday scheduling you can safely use a 9‑hour offset.
message.reasoning: We need to answer: time difference between Los Angeles (Pacific Time) and Berlin (Central European Time). But time difference depends on daylight saving. Los Angeles is UTC-8 standard, UTC-7 DST. Berlin is UTC+1 standard, UTC+2 DST. So difference: standard: 9 hours (Berlin ahead). During DST: Los Angeles UTC-7, Berlin UTC+2 => 9 hours again? Wait: -7 to +2 difference is 9 hours. Actually both shift by one hour, so difference remains 9 hours. But check: In summer, Los Angeles is PDT (UTC-7), Berlin is CEST (UTC+2). Difference 9 hours. In winter, PST (UTC-8), CET (UTC+1). Difference 9 hours. So constant 9 hours. But if one is in DST and other not? That could happen during transition periods. But generally 9 hours.
